title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-03-01
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: Soundboard‑derived tape with a few audience‑mic hiccups captures a fun 1970 show highlighted by a scorching Cryptical > Other One and the rare “Big Boy Pete.”
ai_review.review: The performance is lively – fans rave about the intense Cryptical > Other One, a solid Big Boy Pete, and strong renditions of Good Lovin', Morning Dew, Black Peter, China Cat > I Know You Rider, Uncle John’s Band and Baby Blue.  The recording is mostly soundboard quality but the first two tracks (and a few seconds later) come from noisy audience mics, the vocals sit a bit high in the mix and some EQ work helps, yet the middle of the set sounds clear enough to enjoy.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise the musical flow and standout songs; recording issues are limited to early tracks and vocal balance, so overall enjoyment is high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First two songs (and a few seconds of the third) are from audience mics and sound rough; throughout the middle the SBD is clear but vocals sit too high in the mix, requiring EQ for optimal balance.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows well, with the rare Big Boy Pete sandwiched between strong mid‑set numbers; transitions such as Cryptical > Other One into Black Peter are praised for their seamlessness.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is generally praised (“intense,” “perfect tone”), though one reviewer notes it could have been a hair louder.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ lines on The Other One are mentioned as not exploding enough; overall keyboard presence is modest but functional for the era.
band_member_comments.Drums: Good Lovin' drums receive specific praise; the rhythm section is described as solid throughout.
